name: Weed flat
pro: Broad shallow weed growth, 3 to 10 ft. Fish roam it in low light and when wind pushes bait onto it.
yourJob: Watch for the weed tops under the boat and say when they change.

name: Weed edge
pro: Where the weeds stop against deeper water. The outside edge is the ambush line most of the year.
yourJob: Keep the boat on the edge; call out when the sonar shows weeds ending.

name: Point
pro: Structure that reaches into deep water. Fish stage on the sides the wind loads.
yourJob: Cast across the point, not down it.

name: Inside turn
pro: A pocket in the breakline. Bait collects in it. Big fish sit in the corner.
yourJob: Slow the boat; the fish is in the corner, not the open side.

name: Saddle
pro: A shallow ridge between two deeper areas. Fish cross it on travel routes.

name: Hump
pro: A sunken island. Fish circle it; the deep side is the fall side.
yourJob: Mark the top with the sonar so we fish the whole rim.

name: Break
pro: A sharp depth change. Suspended fish hold off it in fall.
yourJob: Watch the depth number; say when it drops fast.

name: Neck
pro: A channel between lakes. Current, bait, and travel. The chain's necks are its signature structure.
yourJob: Keep the boat out of the channel so we do not spook it.

name: Inlet
pro: Where a creek or lake enters. Cooler, oxygenated water in late summer; bait in fall.
yourJob: Look for current lines on the surface.

name: Outlet
pro: Where the lake drains. Current pulls bait; the dam end of Cisco is one.
yourJob: Watch for the no-boat line near a dam.

name: Rock
pro: Gravel and boulders. Cisco spawn on it in late fall. Holds heat in spring.
yourJob: Say when the sonar bottom goes hard.

name: Wood
pro: Logs and flooded timber from the 1931 raise. Ambush cover.
yourJob: Keep the lure above the wood; count it down.

name: Island
pro: An island's shoreline is a point and a weed edge in one.

name: Shoal
pro: A shallow bar off a shoreline. Steep on this chain: sand, gravel, peat.
yourJob: Watch the trolling motor in the shallows.
